solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Belittle bridge opponents with “mug to lead” (2,4)

indicatorNotes.to lead: the mug goes in front of the bridge players

blocks.note: a mug is a fool, and so is a dodo
West and North sit in opposing partnerships at bridge

annotation.surface: A bridge player sneers at the opponents, putting the table's fool in charge.
annotation.walkthrough: At bridge North partners South and East partners West, so any two neighbouring seats, such as W and N, are opponents.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to disparage someone, make them seem small.

entries.clue: Fine curtailed Trump’s flakiness? (8)

indicatorNotes.curtailed: cut off at the tail: the last letter goes

blocks.note: to ruff is to play a trump card

annotation.surface: A jibe at a certain politician's unreliable temperament.
annotation.walkthrough: Trump's capital letter points at the politician; it is the card-game verb. The question mark flags the playful definition: dandruff is literally flakiness of the scalp.
annotation.definitionFit: Dandruff is flakes of dead skin, so a flaky condition, stretched here with a question mark.
annotation.definitionNote: Flakiness is the condition; dandruff is the flakes themselves.

entries.clue: Trail broken leg, bearing pain (7)

indicatorNotes.broken: the letters of LEG are broken up and rearranged
indicatorNotes.bearing: in a down clue the leg sits below and bears the pain on top of it

blocks.note: a drag is a pain, a tiresome thing

annotation.surface: An injured walker limps along a path with a broken leg, in pain.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Trail' looks like a footpath noun; it is the verb. 'Bearing' works because this is a down clue: the broken leg sits underneath the pain, holding it up.
annotation.definitionFit: To draggle is to trail along behind, or through mud.

entries.clue: Popular Liberal upset butcher in garden (4-5)

indicatorNotes.upset: in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, reversing it
indicatorNotes.in: the Liberal and reversed butcher go inside the garden verb

blocks.note: first half of WEED, to garden

annotation.surface: A well-loved Liberal politician is toppled by a slaughterer in someone's garden.
annotation.walkthrough: Garden and butcher both look like nouns; both are verbs here, to weed and to kill. L plus LLIK makes three L's in a row, which is why the hyphen helps.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both describe someone whom many people like.

entries.clue: Called again about faulty gadget (8)

indicatorNotes.faulty: the gadget's letters are faulty, so out of order

annotation.surface: Someone phones the helpline a second time about a broken gadget.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Called' suggests a phone call; it means named, as a tag names something.
annotation.definitionFit: To tag something is to label or name it, so retagged is renamed, called again.

entries.clue: Actor and journalist on identical charges having pinched fuel (6,8)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue the journalist sits on top of what follows
indicatorNotes.having pinched: the two charges have stolen the fuel and hold it between them

blocks.note: a ward is someone in another's charge

annotation.surface: A news story: an actor and a reporter face the same charges for stealing fuel.
annotation.walkthrough: Edward Woodward was an English actor, star of The Equalizer and The Wicker Man. 'Charges' suggests criminal counts; here they are people in someone's care.
annotation.definitionFit: Edward Woodward was a well-known English actor.

entries.clue: Casual job rejected by great old buffoon (5)

indicatorNotes.rejected by: the casual job is thrown out of the bigger word

blocks.note: a gig is a one-off piece of work, removed from the front

annotation.surface: A pompous old fool turns down some casual work.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Great old' reads as a phrase, but the break comes after 'great': 'old' belongs to the definition, since ANTIC in this sense is archaic.
annotation.definitionFit: An antic was once a clown or grotesque performer, a buffoon.

entries.clue: Coaching failed to yield first-class dumplings (7)

indicatorNotes.failed: the coaching went wrong, so its letters are scrambled
indicatorNotes.to yield: to yield is to surrender something, so the first-class A is handed over and dropped

blocks.note: the anagram fodder before the loss
A = first-class, as in A1; this letter is removed

annotation.surface: Bad cooking lessons meant nobody turned out top-quality dumplings.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a cookery class that went wrong, and gnocchi is exactly what such a class might attempt.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: these Italian potato morsels are one kind of dumpling.

entries.clue: Increase strength of hideaway, covering leak up (6)

indicatorNotes.covering: the hideaway wraps around the leak
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, up means read bottom to top

blocks.note: a den is a hideaway, split around the leak
PEE (slang for a leak, urinating) reversed

annotation.surface: Advice to reinforce a secret shelter by covering a leak in its roof.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leak' is British slang for urinating, as in 'take a leak', so it gives PEE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making a colour, feeling or sound more intense strengthens it.

entries.clue: Enter bar in felt buckles? That’s an embarrassment (6,8)

indicatorNotes.buckles: the phrase buckles out of shape, rearranging its letters

annotation.surface: Someone walks into a pub wearing felt shoes with buckles and is mocked for it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buckles' looks like a noun, fasteners on felt shoes; it is the verb, to bend out of shape.
annotation.definitionFit: An enfant terrible is someone whose outrageous behaviour embarrasses their associates.
annotation.definitionNote: The definition names the effect; the answer is the person who causes it.

entries.clue: Criminal lawyer and con man spoke at last in good nick (6,3)

indicatorNotes.Criminal: the lawyer's letters are crooked, so rearranged
indicatorNotes.at last: take the final letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: last letters of coN, maN, spokE

annotation.surface: A crooked lawyer and a swindler are finally caught and talk in the police station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Criminal lawyer' reads as one job title; 'criminal' is the anagram indicator. 'In good nick' is British for in good condition, while 'nick' also means a police station.
annotation.definitionFit: Something nearly new has hardly been used, so it is in good condition.

entries.clue: Outgoing type stripped twice in store (5)

indicatorNotes.stripped twice: strip off the outer letters, then do it again

blocks.note: an extrovert is an outgoing person

annotation.surface: An extrovert goes wild and undresses in a shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Store' suggests a shop; it means a hoard, as in treasure trove.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of a hoard or cache of valuables.

entries.clue: Bring back one beer to accompany a big cigar (7)

indicatorNotes.Bring back: the whole string is turned round
indicatorNotes.to accompany: the one and the beer go alongside the A

annotation.surface: An order at the bar: bring me a beer to go with my big cigar.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a drinks order, and the cigar belongs in it. Regalia is less familiar as a cigar size than as royal insignia.
annotation.definitionFit: A regalia is a large, high-quality cigar.

entries.clue: Seek further use for components within grey vehicle (7)

indicatorNotes.components within: take the letters found inside the word, dropping its outer ones

annotation.surface: Advice on salvaging parts from an old grey car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Components' reads as car parts to be salvaged; it points to the inner letters of 'grey'.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: processing waste or old goods so they can be used again.

entries.clue: Spot sheep collectively shifting over to middle of field (5)

indicatorNotes.to: the O becomes the letter named next

blocks.note: a flock is a group of sheep
O = over, from cricket scoring; this letter is replaced

annotation.surface: A farmer notices the flock drifting over to the centre of the field.
annotation.walkthrough: O for over comes from cricket scorecards. The surface is a pastoral scene, and the sheep really do move into the field.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tiny mark or speck of colour.

entries.clue: Community has charging point finally switched on (8)

annotation.surface: A village announces that its new electric-car charger is now live.
annotation.walkthrough: The T goes before OWNS even though 'has' comes first in the clue. 'Switched on' looks like the charger working; it means trendy and alert.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym; in South Africa the word also named an area set aside for Black residents under apartheid.

entries.clue: Complaint papers raised ulcer acquired by relative (9)

indicatorNotes.raised: in a down clue, raised means written upwards, reversed
indicatorNotes.acquired by: the relative takes the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: first letter of SIS, a sister

annotation.surface: A newspaper runs a complaint about an ulcer a relative caught.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grievance sent to the papers; it is a medical complaint, an illness.
annotation.definitionFit: Siderosis is a lung disease caused by inhaling iron dust, so a complaint in the medical sense.

entries.clue: One’s inclined to bend the limits of radioisotope dating (8)

indicatorNotes.bend: bend the letters out of order
indicatorNotes.the limits of: only the outer letters of radioisotope are used

blocks.note: first and last letters of RadioisotopE

annotation.surface: A scientist admits to pushing the limits of carbon dating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Radioisotope dating' reads as one technical term; only the ends of the first word and all of the second are needed.
annotation.definitionFit: A slope is literally something inclined, and the 's plays on a person being inclined to do something.

entries.clue: City hospital to decline work (3,5)

blocks.note: to die away is to decline
a machine that goes is working

annotation.surface: A city hospital is going downhill, turning away work.
annotation.walkthrough: SAN, short for sanatorium, is a school-and-crossword word for a hospital or sickbay.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a large port city in southern California.

entries.clue: Pile of workers want to go topless — Benny, for example (7)

indicatorNotes.to go topless: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which goes

annotation.surface: A cheeky comedy sketch in which Benny Hill wants to strip off.
annotation.walkthrough: Benny Hill was a British TV comedian known for saucy slapstick, which is why going topless suits the surface. 'Workers' are ants, as so often.
annotation.definitionFit: An anthill is a heap built by worker ants.

entries.clue: Writer’s miserable doctor tried, having neglected case (5)

indicatorNotes.having neglected case: the outer letters, the case of the word, are left off

blocks.note: HEARD (tried, as a court hears a case) without H…D

annotation.surface: An author is gloomy because the doctor tried to treat him but ignored his case.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer's' marks drear as a literary word rather than everyday speech. 'Case' has a double life: a medical case in the surface, the outside letters in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic form of dreary, miserable.

entries.clue: Loner’s suitable moment to return, before crowds (7)

indicatorNotes.to return: the moment is sent back, reversed
indicatorNotes.crowds: the word for before crowds round the reversed moment

annotation.surface: A recluse judges the right time to come back ahead of the crowds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crowds' looks like a noun, the throngs a loner avoids; it is a verb, squeezing round something. The 's stands for 'is'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an archaic word for a hermit, a religious recluse.

entries.clue: Beautiful actions excuse turning up now and then (6)

indicatorNotes.turning up: in a down clue, turning up means reversing
indicatorNotes.now and then: something done now and then happens only intermittently, so only every other letter is taken

blocks.note: every second letter of aCtIoNs ExCuSe

annotation.surface: Graceful moves that excuse showing up only occasionally.
annotation.walkthrough: Of the alternate-letter sets, only the even ones spell anything backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym, used of views and landscapes that are beautiful to look at.

entries.clue: Drained theatre nurse maybe collars food supplier (7)

indicatorNotes.Drained: emptied of its insides, leaving the outer letters
indicatorNotes.collars: the nurse grabs the drained theatre and holds it

blocks.note: a nurse is one kind of carer

annotation.surface: An exhausted theatre nurse grabs the man supplying the food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Theatre nurse' reads as an operating-theatre job; the phrase splits.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain description: the firm or person who provides food and drink for events.

entries.clue: Partly lifting ottoman is ordinarily a help when varnishing (5)

indicatorNotes.Partly: the answer is part of the words that follow
indicatorNotes.lifting: in a down clue, lifting means read upwards

annotation.surface: Advice that lifting the ottoman usually helps when you are varnishing the floor.
annotation.walkthrough: The furniture-moving surface hides a tree resin that goes into varnish.
annotation.definitionFit: Rosin is a resin used in making varnishes.

entries.clue: Revolutionary Green leader? That could be incendiary (7)

annotation.surface: A radical Green Party leader is branded a firebrand.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital G makes 'Green' look political; it is green meaning raw, inexperienced.
annotation.definitionFit: A warhead is the explosive tip of a missile, and some are incendiary.

entries.clue: Catches slowcoach delaying son’s appearance (5)

indicatorNotes.delaying: the S turns up later, moved to the end

blocks.note: SNAIL (a slowcoach) with its S taken out
S = son, now appearing at the end

annotation.surface: A late-running boy holds up everyone waiting for him.
annotation.walkthrough: The S of SNAIL is not lost, only delayed: it moves from the front to the back.
annotation.definitionFit: To nail someone is to catch them.

entries.clue: Fools lease land west of London (9)

blocks.note: berk is British slang for a fool

annotation.surface: Some foolish people rent a plot of land outside London.
annotation.walkthrough: Berkshire is an English county west of London. Berk is mild British slang for an idiot.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by description: the English county lying just west of Greater London.

entries.clue: Solid shelf delivered with fashionable red backing (8)

indicatorNotes.delivered: spoken, as a speech is delivered

blocks.note: a sill is a shelf; said out loud it matches CYL

annotation.surface: A sturdy shelf arrives with a trendy red back panel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Solid' looks like an adjective describing the shelf; it is the noun, a geometric solid.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: in geometry a solid is a three-dimensional shape, and this is one.

entries.clue: Act like court has sealed the end for MS Outlook (6)

indicatorNotes.has sealed: the imitation and court close round the letter
indicatorNotes.the end for: the end of MS is its final letter

blocks.note: last letter of MS, sealed after the A

annotation.surface: A court seals the fate of Microsoft's email program.
annotation.walkthrough: 'MS Outlook' reads as the Microsoft product, but the phrase splits: MS supplies S and Outlook is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An aspect is an outlook or view, as a south-facing aspect.
